messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: Sampling effort in post stratified data
parts:
Fernanda:

Glad to see you are using what we discussed in Cambridge.

The most common way to think about stratification is geographic: stratum
1 is over there, stratum 2 is over here. Sampling effort is allocated
within geographical strata. When post-stratifying, Distance allocates
effort to each strata; in your case sex. Of course you do not
repeatedly walk transects for each sex. If the factor you were
post-stratifying upon had 3 categories, it would appear as if your
effort had trebled.

Distance is performing the proper calculations: encounter rates (number
of detections [by sex] per unit of transect walked) is calculated
correctly. No need for you to alter your data input.

> > Dear all,

Is this just the way that it outputs the data? Or is it acttually doubling my sampling effort and I should enter it differently to use the post stratification tool?
